title: Audit
meta: Read recorded changes and access events
intro: Audit records who performed an action, when it happened and which entity it affected. Administrators and reviewers use it to investigate changes and access events.
You need View audit log. Use the events already recorded by your installation. The pictures show changes to fictional accounts and layouts in a test installation. No sample data is required.
Audit is read-only. Reading an event does not change it. Before, After and Metadata appear only when that action recorded those values.

tasks.title: Find events for an action
intro: Use this when you know the kind of action you need to investigate. You can also filter by actor, entity or time.
steps: Read When, Actor, Action, Entity type and Entity ID. An action such as user.update describes the recorded operation.
Open the column selector and choose Action. Keep Equals for an exact action name.
Enter the action to inspect. The example uses user.update for profile changes. Use an action present in your own installation.
tasks.result: The list shows matching events. An empty result means no event matches the current rules.

tasks.title: Read an event and its recorded values
intro: Use this to identify the affected record and compare changes. Different actions record different details.
steps: Select the matching event row. Read the event identifier, timestamp, actor, action and affected entity in the sheet.
Scroll to Before. It contains previous values when the action supplied them. None recorded. means no snapshot was recorded.
Scroll to After. Compare the saved values with Before. These are recorded snapshots, not an editor.
Scroll to Metadata for any additional recorded context.
Copy an event reference when needed
Use Copy Event ID beside the identifier when recording a reference in your investigation. Other populated detail values also have copy controls.
tasks.result: You return to the same filtered event list. The audit record remains unchanged.

tasks.title: Browse more events and refresh the list
intro: Use this when you need events outside the current page or changes recorded after you opened Audit.
steps: Open Filter and select Clear to return to all events.
Open Rows per page at the bottom and select a size. The example chooses 10.
Select Next page when it is enabled.
Open the page dots and select Refresh. The current filters still apply.
tasks.result: The table reads the requested page or refreshed events from the server.

tasks.title: Read audit events on a phone
intro: Use the same Audit page on a phone. The event table can scroll horizontally.
steps: Use Filter above the table to narrow the results before reading wide rows.
Select an event row. Scroll the sheet to read identifiers and snapshots.

end.title: Optional practice
paragraphs: In a test installation, make an approved profile or layout change, then find its audit event. Compare the recorded Before and After values when present. No audit-data import is required.

end.title: Limits
paragraphs: This page does not edit, delete or export audit events. A missing snapshot does not prove that an action made no change. It means that action recorded no snapshot.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: No audit events match. Review the active filter chips or choose Filter, then Clear.
A recent event is absent. Choose Refresh and check the current filters and page.
Before or After says None recorded. Use the actor, action, entity details and available metadata. That snapshot cannot be recovered through this page.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Read Users for account actions and Roles for permissions. Read Start here for command-line setup.
